assessment: No security finding was established in the fully reviewed web executable source or the inspected bridge boundary. This conclusion depends on backend authorization and the source-backed deployment assumptions; it does not attest live configuration or dependency security.

resolved_questions.question: Can browser headers choose the upstream destination or receive the transport key?
resolved_questions.answer: Rejected. backendOrigin derives its destination exclusively from server environment, validates scheme/authority/path and disables Vercel loopback use. Proxy requests build a fresh header set rather than forwarding browser Authorization or forwarding headers. LASTCOPY_TRANSPORT_KEY appears only in server helpers/routes; the layout passes only a cloud-enabled boolean to the client.

resolved_questions.question: Do sibling proxy routes bypass write-origin or action restrictions?
resolved_questions.answer: Rejected. Service, account and session POST routes validate Host and write Origin before forwarding. Account/session actions are explicit lists with 2 KiB bodies. Demo allows only fixed cases and method/action combinations, with POST Origin validation. Inventory/examples routes have fixed read targets and are not arbitrary upstream proxies.
resolved_questions.counterevidence_or_limit: Local mode intentionally permits absent Origin for compatible local callers. Hosted mode requires the configured exact Origin. Browsers cannot freely set Host; the backend independently enforces session authorization.

resolved_questions.question: Can encoded path segments escape service or demo route allowlists?
resolved_questions.answer: No reachable bypass established. Service rejects empty, dot/dot-dot, slash and backslash segments, checks the joined route against an anchored allowlist, and encodes each segment when constructing upstream URLs. Demo performs equivalent segment/route checks and permits POST only for readback.

resolved_questions.question: Do untrusted XML, receipt values or model diagnostics reach raw HTML/script sinks?
resolved_questions.answer: Rejected for inspected web source. Evidence values, paths, receipts, errors, provider diagnostics and run events render through ordinary React text expressions or JSON.stringify inside pre/code elements. There are no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, eval or dynamic Function sinks in the inspected TS/TSX source. Dynamic evidence/download links use internal fixed prefixes and backend object identities.
resolved_questions.counterevidence_or_limit: Production CSP includes unsafe-inline for scripts/styles and therefore is not a substitute for safe rendering. No concrete injection sink was established, so this was not promoted into a CSP vulnerability.

resolved_questions.question: Can a user-controlled return path navigate to an external destination?
resolved_questions.answer: Rejected. ownerReturn permits only a small set of anchored product-owned routes. Login sanitizes next before passing it to AccountForm or constructing the configured-workspace redirect. Workspace origins must be HTTPS origins without credentials, path, query or fragment.

resolved_questions.question: Are credentials exposed in browser storage, URLs or returned setup state?
resolved_questions.answer: No exposure established in inspected browser code. Password/API-key forms send JSON to same-origin routes and clear credential inputs after submission. There is no localStorage/sessionStorage/document.cookie use. Only the session cookie is forwarded upstream; account-auth requests explicitly discard an existing Cookie header. Backend session creation owns Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie attributes.

resolved_questions.question: Does requireOwner grant private access when its settings probe fails?
resolved_questions.answer: The helper redirects on missing cookie/configuration or backend 401, but permits rendering a static shell on other backend status/errors. This does not establish data exposure: private pages render client components without server-fetched evidence, and those components call the independently protected API. Backend CloudAccess/account-store selection still determines every evidence operation.

resolved_questions.question: Can a beta account obtain owner-only provider setup by visiting /integrations or using the service route?
resolved_questions.answer: The page guard accepts any valid hosted session and exposes a generic settings shell, but backend cloud_ai.owner independently validates the root owner session. The account-selected evidence store does not confer operator credentials. No privilege increase was established in the web route.

resolved_questions.question: Can public examples or demo downloads access private account/owner evidence through forwarded cookies?
resolved_questions.answer: Rejected. The demo proxy strips cookies and permits only fixed paths; backend demo workspace constructs a separate public-examples store with sample-only Settings. The earlier examples route forwards shaped cookies, but the backend implementation explicitly constructs the same separate sample-only store rather than selecting private evidence from that cookie.

resolved_questions.question: Do imported XML/media execute inline through download responses?
resolved_questions.answer: No path was established. The client uses download links rather than embedding imported source as HTML/image/frame content. The service proxy relays only selected response headers and applies no-store/nosniff. Backend evidence-object responses use application/octet-stream and nosniff.

resolved_questions.question: Can model-controlled actions or graph state invoke arbitrary reference-library methods, filesystem writes or recovery?
resolved_questions.answer: No such capability was established in the inspected integration. Model output validates against a strict action enum and a phase-specific allowlist. Coordinator code writes typed evidence-backed journal records and invokes one fixed Node/tsx bridge using bounded JSON stdin. Both bridges instantiate memory storage with fixed namespaces. EventStore's filesystem persistence branch activates only for storage=local and is not selected by these callers. The connected coordinator compares query rows against its own scoped evidence and computes deterministic verdicts itself.
resolved_questions.counterevidence_or_limit: This is a focused integration review, not a full security audit of every vendored library operation or its standalone local-storage consumers.

resolved_questions.question: Are Vercel gateway behavior and deployment protections independently proven?
resolved_questions.answer: Only source behavior is established. Private service/account/session routes reject gateway operation; fixed public demo/example routes remain usable if backend configuration remains present. No private evidence crossover was found, but current WORKSPACE_ORIGIN, API_ORIGIN, transport-key retention, CSP headers and reverse-proxy behavior require deployment evidence.

partial_or_triage_only.disposition: Reviewed actual bridge methods, memory-store construction, journal integrity/bounds, model phase allowlists, query-row validation and deterministic comparison callers; not marked whole-file audited.
Inventory/search only; full vendored-library audit was outside the optional focused integration pass.

structurally_reviewed_files.disposition: Complete structural review of all 4,390 declaration lines after stripping comments/string literals: exactly three top-level interfaces (paths/components/operations), two aliases (webhooks/$defs), balanced 821 opening/closing braces, no function bodies/imports/require/classes/variables/enums/namespaces/runtime control flow/arrows/template literals or runtime assignments. The only equals signs define the two type aliases. The only executable-looking keyword matches are delete?: never property declarations. All six runtime-source references are explicit import type; package.json reference is the generator output command. Declaration-only structural verification, not executable line audit.

excluded_binary_files.disposition: Font binary reverse-engineering excluded. Local serving, SIL OFL 1.1 license, pinned Google Fonts source metadata, length 20,352 and exact SHA-256 match to sources.json verified offline.
Font binary reverse-engineering excluded. Local serving, SIL OFL 1.1 license, pinned Google Fonts source metadata, length 22,948 and exact SHA-256 match to sources.json verified offline.

static_css.disposition: Full source text reviewed for every stylesheet, including rule-expanded display of minified source. CSS contains fixed local layout/state/presentation rules, same-origin font URLs and one fixed data-SVG select icon. No external fetch/import, expression, JavaScript URL, behavior binding, dynamic attribute-to-URL or caller-supplied style construction was established. State-dependent rules change presentation only.

replay_exports.disposition: Full parsed object reviewed, including every key and string leaf, all events/queries/report receipts/world revisions. Opaque 64-hex digests normalized for display; all meaningful strings retained. Static Replay contains authored synthetic inspection/uuid:41-a identifiers, XML paths, media-slot filenames, query SQL and hashes, model identity/usage and non-executable guidance. No archive/XML/media byte payload, account credential, provider authorization or secret URL was established. File hash and report-hash reference match sponsor-replays.json; synthetic provenance supported by export generator and fixture construction.

fonts.disposition: Both complete license files and metadata read. Browser loads same-origin /fonts/*.woff2 via fixed CSS/font preloads, with no remote font service. Actual local sizes/hashes match manifest; this does not authenticate upstream provenance independently or audit font parser behavior.

limitations: No application execution, browser interaction, network access, dependency/CVE audit or exploit input was performed.
Only the explicitly authorized temporary architecture and web-review artifacts were written; source was not edited.
Generated API declarations received complete structural verification; bundled font binaries were hash/size/provenance checked but not reverse-engineered.
No confirmed finding does not establish live-deployment safety. Runtime configuration, framework behavior under deployment and the partially reviewed vendored-library files remain limitations.
